To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ZnO nanofiber mats can be fabricated through electrospinning and calcination of ZnO/PVA precursors.

the electrospinning of zinc acetate and PVA precursor has been successfully employed for the synthesis of ZnO nanowires with a diameter range of 100 to 500 nm and the average diameter was increased with an increase in the content of zinc precursors.
ZnO nano fibers were successfully synthesized using electrospinning method.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of 1D ZnO nanofiber mat through electrospinning technique.
the development of ZnO nanomaterials and its applications in the renewable solar energy.
the fabrication and characterization of ZnO nanowires for renewable energy applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ZnO nanofiber mats were successfully fabricated by electrospinning of PVA and zinc acetate precursor and calcination at 480 °C.
the electrospun ZnO nanofiber mats have been successfully fabricated by sol-gel processing and electrospining of PVA and zinc acetate precursor.
the ZnO nanowires were fabricated by the electrospinning of the zinc acetated PVA solution and the calcination at 480 °C.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electrospinning of ZnO precursor has been found to have a significant effect in the morphology of the ZnO nanostructures.
the ZnO nanorods can be fabricated by electrospinning and calcination of ZnO/PVA precursor at 480 °C.
the ZnO nanomaterials are synthesized through electrospinning and the ZnO nanowires are fabricated by calcination of the ZnO/PVA precursor nanofibers at 480 °C.
The main takeaway from our work is that

ZnO nanofiber can be used as a photoanode in dye-sensitized solar cells (DSC) to improve the power conversion efficiency (η) and fill factor (FF) by reducing the recombination rate of electrons at the ZnO/electrolyte interface.
ZnO nanofiber mat can be used as transparent conductors in the photovoltaic applications.
ZnO nanofiber mats can be fabricated by electrospinning of PVA and zinc acetate precursor and calcined at 480 °C to obtain bead-free smooth nanofibres.
